proposals.relationship: Wedgwood names Marc Bloch among the historians who influenced her historical practice.
proposals.evidence_note: Own signed 1960 essay, printed 6, column 1, opening paragraph. Her explicit retrospective acknowledgment names several historians and gives Burckhardt the strongest emphasis; it does not identify a particular Bloch book, doctrine or personal encounter. The original works named elsewhere in the essay remain unread.
primary_locators: AJR Information XV:3 (March 1960):6, column 1, opening paragraph

proposals.relationship: Stone criticizes Wedgwood’s regicide narrative for insufficient political explanation and dramatic reconstruction that, in his judgment, distorts the evidence.
proposals.evidence_note: Complete signed original 1964 review, paragraphs beginning “One wonders”, “How far”, “If Miss Wedgwood”, and “The objection”. Stone praises her narrative skill while questioning treatment of the Army, the regicides and the execution’s consequences. These are his criticisms of A Coffin for King Charles, not independently verified errors or a rejection of every narrative history. The reviewed book and archival evidence remain unread.
primary_locators: NYRB 10 September 1964, History à la Mode, complete displayed review; paragraphs 3–5 and 7–10 of review body
